title: Pharmacy Operations Standard: Automated Refill Cycles under Auto Refill & Medication Sync
content:
An automated cycle of an Auto Refill & Medication Sync enrollment is scheduled only while the enrollment is in active status, except the first cycle, which is scheduled at activation, when the enrollment moves from enrolled to active. The status is the one shown on that enrollment's own record before the cycle is queued. Each scheduled cycle carries the date it is due and the days supply it will dispense.

## 1. Cycle date

1.1 Where the program's cycle date is set by the last fill date, the cycle date is the prescription's refill-eligible date under the Prescriptions charter.

1.2 Where the program's cycle date is set by the sync day, the cycle date is the next sync day on or after that refill-eligible date.

Cases on a sync day of the 20th (hypothetical):

| Refill-eligible date | Cycle date |
|---|---|
| 14 March | 20 March |
| 20 March | 20 March (the sync day falls on the refill-eligible date itself) |
| 22 March | 20 April |

## 2. Processing date

2.1 The refill is processed the program's refill lead time, in calendar days, before the cycle date. For adherence packs, the packaging preparation days are added to that lead time, so the refill is processed the lead time plus the preparation days before the cycle date.

2.2 Worked figures (hypothetical inputs): for a cycle date of 20 June, a lead time of 7 calendar days gives a processing date of 13 June. A lead time of 10 calendar days together with 3 packaging preparation days makes 13 calendar days, giving a processing date of 7 June.

## 3. Supply dispensed

Each cycle dispenses the program's days supply per cycle, never more than the prescription's class and coverage allow.

## 4. Short fills to the sync day

4.1 Where the program allows short fills to the sync day and the prescription's next due date is at least the program's short-fill minimum number of days before the sync day, a short fill covering exactly the days to the sync day is dispensed and the cycle is marked as a sync short fill.

4.2 Where the program prorates the copay on short fills, the patient pays the copay prorated by those days: the copay multiplied by the number of short-fill days and divided by the program's days supply per cycle, rounded to the cent, half up.

4.3 Where fewer days than the minimum remain to the sync day, they are carried to the following sync day.

Worked short fills (hypothetical inputs; sync day the 20th, short-fill minimum taken as 3 days, days supply per cycle taken as 30):

| Next due date | Days to the sync day | Outcome | Prorated copay |
|---|---|---|---|
| 12 May | 8 | Short fill of 8 days | On a copay of $12.00: 12.00 multiplied by 8, divided by 30, is $3.20 |
| 15 May | 5 | Short fill of 5 days | On a copay of $3.15: 3.15 multiplied by 5, divided by 30, is 0.525, rounded half up to $0.53 |
| 17 May | 3 | Short fill of 3 days (exactly the minimum) | Prorated in the same way |
| 18 May | 2 | No short fill; carried to the following sync day | — |

## 5. Filling a cycle once

A cycle is filled only once and only after any required confirmation. A cycle that already has a fill or a skip recorded against it is not filled; the check is made on that cycle's own entries before it is filled. A filled cycle is dispensed as a fill of the prescription.

## 6. Where cycles are dispensed and how they travel

Cycles are dispensed at the program's dispensing location — the store holding the prescription, or central fill — and, where the enrollment is set to home delivery, delivered at the program's delivery speed.

## 7. Offer of the 90-day program

After the program's stated number of filled cycles, where that number is above 0, Kestrel offers the patient the 90-day program; the patient decides.
